children: German day-ahead power prices rose on Monday as wind and to a lesser extent solar power generation fell, while consumption was expected to rise.
Germany's day-ahead baseload contract (TRDEBD1) was up 30% from the closing price for the previous day, to €145.50 ($168.58) per megawatt hour at 0731 GMT.
Consumption in Germany is expected to rise by 1.6 gigawatts to 51.8 GW, while wind and solar power generation are expected to drop by 2.1 GW and 0.8 GW respectively.

"German output falling to around 12 GW from 20 GW tomorrow before recovering towards the end of the week, while French wind could drop to around 2 GW starting tomorrow," analysts at Engie's EnergyScan wrote in a note.
The equivalent French contract (TRFRBD1) was not traded, according to LSEG data.
French wind power generation is expected to fall 7.9 GW to 1.8 GW while solar power is expected to remain largely stable at 6.2 GW. Consumption is set to rise by 1.9 GW to 44.8 GW.
French nuclear availability fell by 2 percentage points to 76% of total availability.
On the forward side, the German year-ahead contract (TRDEBYc1) was marginally up by 0.3% to €115.25, establishing a new high since November 2023.
"The gas market is rallying amid the rising Middle East tensions we have seen over the weekend," Mind Energy analysts said in a note.

U.S. President Donald Trump posted an AI-generated video clip that he said showed Iran's oil hub Kharg Island being blown to smithereens, which an Iranian official dismissed as "laughable", just hours after both nations resumed hostilities for the first time since July.
The equivalent French contract (TRFRBYc1) was not traded, according to LSEG data.
The European carbon market's benchmark contract
edged down 0.42% to €82.38 a metric ton.
